Presently, students in the School of Professional Studies, URI’s School that primarily serves STAR (service-member, transfer, adult, and returning) students, need to decide between two bachelor’s of science degree programs: Nonprofit Administration and Professional Leadership Studies.
Although the programs’ courses are synergistic and students have an interest in exploring topics from both programs, these programs require students to take a strict set of courses.

Ultimately, there is little room for students to take courses in the other program from their major.
From a student perspective, this is limiting their opportunities for learning.
From a School perspective, this is increasing our difficulty to fill courses and best serve our students.
Our objective with this proposal is to provide greater flexibility for our students as a way to enhance their academic experience and establish more streamlined approaches for students to graduate.
By approving this proposal, the Professional Leadership Studies program would require students to take five courses as “major requirements” (15 credits).
Of these core courses, four of them would fulfill both majors.
One of them, SPC 420: Facilitating Leadership Development, would be the gateway course for the Professional Leadership Studies major designation.
